payload.rationale: The obligation asks two coupled questions: (1) whether the Part I.A oil/solids prohibition is a purely qualitative effluent limitation not subject to numeric DMR compliance comparison, and (2) the scope of covered substances and assessment locations (discharge point versus receiving water or stream banks). On qualitative character, the nominated clause itself states only visibility-based prohibitions with no numeric limits (page 5), and the packet's page-4 Part I.A excerpt shows only Whole Effluent Toxicity parameters with Report values, not numeric limits for floating solids, foam, or oil. However, page 6 generically ties Part I.A to daily-maximum and monthly-average DMR exceedance reporting without distinguishing which Part I.A limits are numeric, and the packet does not include the full Part I.A monitoring table for the floating-solids/foam/oil parameters. That gap prevents grounded closure that this clause is excluded from numeric comparison. On scope, the clause names substances (floating solids, visible foam, oil films, globules, grease, solids) but assessment location is internally ambiguous: the prohibition targets conditions in or on the water and coatings on stream banks, while the adjacent sample-collection sentence requires samples at the discharge after treatment and before the receiving stream for monitoring requirements specified above—yet the FLOATING SOLIDS section excerpt does not define explicit monitoring frequencies or tie those requirements clearly to the qualitative prohibitions. Reconciling whether compliance is judged at point of discharge, in the receiving water, or on stream banks therefore exceeds what the packet establishes. Per P5, neither ACCEPT (affirmative resolution of both questions) nor REJECT (established contrary resolution) is sufficiently grounded; UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
